title: Manus parent Butterfly Effect raises $500M+ after Beijing unwound Meta deal
subtitle: Boyu and IDG led the first funding round since China's planning agency killed a $2B Meta acquisition in April, with Tencent, HSG, and ZhenFund re-upping.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Butterfly Effect, the Chinese startup behind the Manus general-purpose AI agent, closed a funding round of more than $500 million on October 8 — its first since a $2 billion acquisition by Meta was ordered unwound by China's planning agency in April. Boyu Capital and IDG Capital led the round, with existing investors Tencent, HSG (formerly Sequoia China), and ZhenFund participating. The company did not disclose the valuation; Bloomberg has previously reported a $4 billion target. Manus is also reported to be weighing a Hong Kong listing.

The round matters because of what Beijing undid to get here. In December 2025, Meta announced it would absorb Butterfly Effect for roughly $2 billion. On April 27, China's National Development and Reform Commission ordered the deal reversed on national-security and data-flow grounds, and Manus resumed independent operations in August. The $500M round is the market's answer: capital is still available to a Chinese agent startup that explicitly uses Anthropic's Claude and fine-tuned Alibaba Qwen models alongside its own stack, even without a U.S. hyperscaler acquirer. It is the clearest demonstration this year that Chinese AI capital markets can finance frontier-agent companies independently.

Manus itself is one of the most-watched agent products of 2026. Its pitch is not "chatbot that answers questions" but "software that takes a goal — book this trip, analyze this stock, build this spreadsheet — and carries it out," and its mixed-model architecture (foreign frontier models plus local open-weight fine-tunes) has become a template others in China are copying. The funding will go toward compute, hiring at home and abroad, and the next generation of the agent. In context, this is the third nine-figure round for a Chinese agent company in six weeks, after Zhipu and MiniMax earlier in the quarter.

The learner's takeaway: in agent economics, 2026 is proving that "compute access" and "model access" are no longer the only moats worth watching. Butterfly Effect raised more than most pure-model startups do, on the strength of a product that routes work across whichever model happens to be best for each sub-task. For anyone building with AI, that's the real signal — the companies winning right now are the ones that treat frontier models as interchangeable inputs and compete on orchestration, workflow design, and user trust.
